name: Stoneclad Smokeshow Chicken
sub: Smoky, bone-in chicken leg quarters roasted over root vegetables in stoneware, with savory pan juices.
text:
THE STORY
David had been using plenty of liquid smoke and smoked salt in his cooking. When we built this chicken-and-vegetable roast in a Pampered Chef stoneware baking dish, his AI kitchen collaborator dubbed it Stoneclad Smokeshow Chicken: stoneclad for the baking dish, smokeshow for all that smoky flavor. The name stuck, and here it is, immortalized in the cookbook.

INGREDIENTS
4 bone-in, skin-on chicken leg quarters, 1-1 1/2 lb each (5 lb total assumed for nutrition)
10 oz red potatoes, cut into chunks
1 lb sweet potato, cut into chunks
6 oz carrots, chopped
8 oz celery, chopped
6 1/2 oz onion, chopped
2 tsp olive oil
1 cup prepared chicken bouillon
1 tsp unflavored powdered gelatin, optional
1 Tbsp cold water, for blooming the optional gelatin
Worcestershire sauce, to taste
Smoked paprika, to taste
Garlic powder, to taste
Smoked salt, to taste
Black pepper, to taste
Onion powder, to taste
Thyme, to taste

DIRECTIONS
1. Heat the oven to 400 F. Use oven-safe stoneware according to its manufacturer's directions, including any preheating and temperature-change precautions.
2. Cut the potatoes, sweet potato, carrots, celery, and onion into reasonably uniform pieces. Toss with the olive oil and season with smoked paprika, garlic powder, smoked salt, black pepper, and thyme.
3. Spread the vegetables in a large stoneware baking pan. Roast uncovered for 20-25 minutes to give the denser vegetables a head start.
4. Pat the chicken leg quarters dry. Season all over with smoked paprika, garlic powder, smoked salt, black pepper, onion powder, and thyme. Arrange skin-side up over the vegetables without overlapping.
5. Add the prepared bouillon and Worcestershire sauce around the chicken, keeping the skin above the liquid. Follow the stoneware manufacturer's guidance when adding liquid to a hot dish.
6. Roast uncovered for about 50-70 minutes after adding the chicken, until the vegetables are tender and the chicken is cooked through. Large quarters may take longer; use a thermometer rather than time alone. Check the thickest part of both thigh and drumstick without touching bone. Chicken must reach at least 165 F; leg quarters are usually more tender at 175-185 F.
7. Transfer the chicken to a platter and rest for 5-10 minutes. If the vegetables need longer, return them to the oven while the chicken rests.
8. For lightly thickened pan juices, sprinkle the optional gelatin over the cold water and let it bloom for about 5 minutes. Transfer the hot pan liquid to a saucepan and stir in the bloomed gelatin until dissolved. Gelatin adds body as the liquid cools; it does not make a flour-thickened gravy.
9. Serve the chicken over the roasted vegetables with the pan juices spooned around it.

NOTES
This restores the bone-in leg-quarter style of David's original Stoneclad Smokeshow Chicken, roasted with vegetables in stoneware.
The ingredient amounts are flexible. Adjust the chicken, vegetables, seasonings, and proportions to suit your taste, the number of people you are feeding, and what you have on hand. This recipe is a framework rather than a rigid formula.
Seasonings are intentionally listed to taste. Bouillon, Worcestershire sauce, and smoked salt all contribute sodium.
The chicken weight includes bones and skin. Serving size depends on the size of the quarters and how the cooked meat is divided.

NUTRITION
Estimated whole batch: 4,396 calories · 289.7 g protein · 180.4 g carbohydrates · 274.7 g fat · 30.0 g fiber · 150.4 g net carbohydrates.

Per serving, based on 4 servings (one quarter plus one fourth of the vegetables and pan juices): 1,099 calories · 72.4 g protein · 45.1 g carbohydrates · 68.7 g fat · 7.5 g fiber · 37.6 g net carbohydrates.

Estimated using four raw bone-in, skin-on quarters at the midpoint of 1-1 1/2 lb each: 1 1/4 lb per quarter, 5 lb total. USDA raw chicken leg meat-and-skin data with 27% bone excluded is used as a proxy for leg quarters. Assumes all skin and rendered fat are eaten, including fat retained in the vegetables and pan juices. Uses the listed vegetables, 2 tsp olive oil (9 g), and a generic cup of prepared bouillon (10 calories, 1 g protein, 1 g carbohydrate). Excludes optional gelatin and unmeasured sauces and seasonings. Actual calories and fat will be lower if skin or rendered fat is discarded. Sodium is not estimated because bouillon brand and salt and sauce amounts are unspecified.
